newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Calls via Internet cheaper - OzEmail.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Calls via Internet cheaper - OzEmail.

text.p: Internet service provider OzEmail Ltd said on Thursday its plans to launch telephone service through the Internet could reduce the price of telephone calls.

OzEmail chief executive officer Shaun Howard said the price of telephone calls through the Internet could be only a quarter of those provided by existing telephone companies, state-ownes Telstra Corp and Optus Communications.
OzEmail launched the service with former Australian prime minister Paul Keating making the first call to Mark Roberts, telecommunications analyst at Montgomery Securities in the United States.
"Today, I am pleased to launch what I am confident will become one of the major means by which we will communicate with the rest of the world," Keating told reporters at the launch.
Under Keating's term as prime minister, which ended in March 1996, Australian started the partial deregulation of the local telecoms industry, which will become fully deregulated on July 1, 1997.
The current Coalition government of Prime Minister John Howard is also planning to sell a third of Telstra.
OzEmail's Howard said the group, which is listed on NASDAQ, had about a three to six month start on some of its competitors in this telephony technology for the Internet.
"Calls over the Internet are less expensive because of the superior bandwidth utilisation of the Internet as compared to the traditional technology employed by telephone companies," Howard said.
Howard said the technology was developed with Melbourne based company Interlink Electronics. He said the service would be available only to the company's existing customers.
